title: Etale localization containing the relative assassin detects dimension-filtered flatness
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Use chartwise local finite type and local finite presentation [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact, with quasi-compact diagonal. A module of finite type is locally finitely generated on etale scheme charts; a finitely presented module has locally an exact presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to M\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Let $f:X\to Y$ have scheme base $Y$, be locally of finite type, let $M$ be a finite type quasi-coherent module, and let $h:X\prime\to X$ be representable etale. Put $M\prime=h^*M$. For a scheme $B\to Y$, write $X_B=X\times_YB$ and $M_B$ for tensor pullback. For an integer $n\geq0$, let $P_n(X,M;B)$ mean that for every representable etale scheme chart $a:U\to X_B$ and $u\in U$ mapping to $v\in B$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(v)}\kappa(u)\geq n$, the stalk $(a^*M_B)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{B,v}$. Residue fields, transcendence degree and base-flatness are [def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Use the relative assassin on spaces [def-sfb-space-universal-relative-purity]: $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/Y}(M)$ is the union of the images of the fibrewise associated points on representable etale scheme charts, with scheme associated points as in [def-trf-relative-assassin]. For every scheme $B\to Y$, $P_n(X,M;B)$ implies $P_n(X\prime,M\prime;B)$. If $h(|X\prime|)$ contains $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/Y}(M)$, then for every scheme $B\to Y$ one has $P_n(X,M;B)\Longleftrightarrow P_n(X\prime,M\prime;B)$.

proof.text: For each etale scheme chart, interpret the restriction of $M$ as a Zariski quasi-coherent module using [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Use [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] for composition of all tensor pullbacks. The comparison in the former node identifies these with ordinary scheme pullbacks. Finite type is preserved: a local surjection $\mathcal O^r\twoheadrightarrow N$ pulls back to the surjection $\mathcal O^r\twoheadrightarrow g^*N$, because tensor pullback is a left adjoint and hence right exact. Thus all chart modules used below are finite type quasi-coherent modules; for ordinary scheme base changes quasi-coherence also follows from [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent].

source.place: Tag 0CX0 (lemma-localize-flat-dimension-n), chart modules; scheme/Zariski identifications supplied by Tags 03DX and 03LC.

proof.text: Fix any scheme $B\to Y$. If $P_n(X,M;B)$ holds, any chart $A\to X\prime_B$ composes with $h_B$ to a representable etale chart $A\to X_B$ by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Its map to $B$ is the same composite in both descriptions, so the residue-field degree used in $P_n$ is identical. The tensor-composition identification of step 1 identifies the two module stalks. The asserted flatness on $A$ follows directly from $P_n(X,M;B)$, proving the forward implication without an assassin hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0CX0 (lemma-localize-flat-dimension-n), inclusion of functors, by composition of charts.

proof.text: Assume the image hypothesis. Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p:U\to X$ from a scheme, as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], and put $N=p^*M$. Form $W=U\times_X X\prime$. Since $h$ is representable etale, $W$ is a scheme and $q:W\to U$ is etale; $W\to X\prime$ is a surjective etale chart, by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Every $a\in\operatorname{Ass}_{U/Y}(N)$ maps into $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/Y}(M)$ by the union-of-chart-images definition in the statement. The image hypothesis and the fibre-product image equality of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] therefore imply $a\in q(W)$. Thus $q(W)$ contains the entire scheme relative assassin. No universal-purity or quasi-separatedness assumption has been used.

source.place: Tag 0CX0 (lemma-localize-flat-dimension-n), choice of scheme charts; image comparison via Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian).

proof.text: Continue with the arbitrary $B\to Y$, and put $U_B=U\times_YB$, $W_B=W\times_YB$, $N_B=\operatorname{pr}_U^*N$, $q_B:W_B\to U_B$. These are scheme charts over $X_B$ and $X\prime_B$, and $q_B$ is etale by the base-change assertion of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The map $U\to Y$ is locally of finite type by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], and $U_B\to B$ has the same property by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. The modules are finite type quasi-coherent by step 1. By [lem-sfb-space-dimension-flatness-base-change-sheaf], it suffices for $P_n(X,M;B)$ to verify the ordinary stalk condition on the single surjective atlas $U_B\to X_B$. If $P_n(X\prime,M\prime;B)$ holds, its definition already gives that stalk condition on $W_B\to X\prime_B$.

source.place: Tag 0CX0 (lemma-localize-flat-dimension-n), reduction to scheme functors; Tag 0CWS (lemma-pre-flat-dimension-n), some-atlas/every-chart equivalence.

proof.text: For any $b\in B$ and any associated point $a$ of $(N_B)_b$ on $(U_B)_b$, [lem-trf-relative-assassin-base-change] applied to $U\to Y$, $N$, and $B\to Y$ shows that its image $a_0\in U$ belongs to $\operatorname{Ass}_{U/Y}(N)$. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1 and 4 and it allows an arbitrary base morphism. Step 3 puts $a_0$ in $q(W)$. The fibre-product image equality in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], applied to $W\to U$ and $U_B\to U$, now provides $w\in W_B$ with $q_B(w)=a$. Thus the needed fibre-associated points are covered even after this arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 05UD (lemma-localize-flat-dimension-n), use of Tag 05DC (lemma-base-change-relative-assassin); point lifting is Tag 03H4.

proof.text: Let $u\in U_B$ lie over $b\in B$ and satisfy $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(u)\geq n$. Let $a\in\operatorname{Ass}_{(U_B)_b}((N_B)_b)$ specialize to $u$ in this fibre. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change] the fibre is locally of finite type over $\kappa(b)$. If $a=u$ its transcendence degree is unchanged; otherwise [lem-sfb-field-specialization-trdeg-drop] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(a)>\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(u)$. Lift $a$ to $w\in W_B$ by step 5. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable] the extension $\kappa(w)/\kappa(a)$ is algebraic, so [lem-sbc-transcendence-degree-tower] gives equal transcendence degrees over $\kappa(b)$, in particular at least $n$. The stalk on $W_B$ is therefore $B$-flat by $P_n(X\prime,M\prime;B)$. Since $q_B$ is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], [lem-trf-relative-flatness-source-cover] reflects that flatness to $(N_B)_a$. This verifies flatness at every fibre-associated generalization of $u$.

source.place: Tag 05UD (lemma-localize-flat-dimension-n), associated-point argument, written pointwise using Tag 06RU (lemma-dimension-fibre-specialization) instead of the bad-locus dimension formulation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-flatness-associated-generizations] to $U_B\to B$, $N_B$, and $u$: local finite type and finite type quasi-coherence were checked in step 4, and step 6 verifies its entire associated-generalization condition over the same local ring $\mathcal O_{B,b}$. It follows that $(N_B)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{B,b}$. Since $u$ was arbitrary with the required degree bound, the single-atlas equivalence [lem-sfb-space-dimension-flatness-base-change-sheaf] gives $P_n(X,M;B)$. Together with step 2 this proves the equivalence for every scheme $B\to Y$.

source.place: Tag 05UD (lemma-localize-flat-dimension-n), final application of Tag 05UA (theorem-check-flatness-at-associated-points); chart conclusion as in Tag 0CX0.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0CX0 (lemma-localize-flat-dimension-n), using the proof of flat.tex Tag 05UD (lemma-localize-flat-dimension-n); its associated-point argument is written directly with transcendence degrees and Tag 06RU.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q118-f9d4cb34b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS with no fixes. I read the item, the new node, every cited statement and the Stacks sources: 0CX0, 05UD, 05UA, and 05DC with its remark. The item's statement and stmt_deps match live exactly. On live the item is still unsplit, so no other group has taken it. The 7 steps follow the source route: step 4 reduces to one atlas (0CWS, via the existing node lem-sfb-space-dimension-flatness-base-change-sheaf), then steps 5-7 run the 05UD argument in the item's transcendence-degree terms. Ass coverage after an arbitrary base change uses only the forward direction of 05DC plus the fibre-product image equality. The degree is kept using 06RU (a strict drop under specialization), 02G8 (etale residue extensions are algebraic) and 030H (the transcendence-degree tower). Flatness at w on the chart of X' is reflected to a by flat permanence 02JZ (same base B, same O_{B,b}). Step 7 applies 05UA. Every hypothesis was checked at the step where it is used: local finite type of U->Y via the chart test with V=Y, finite type kept by right exactness of pullback, and W a scheme with q etale. The new node lem-sfb-scheme-flatness-associated-generizations matches 05UA hypothesis by hypothesis. It is statement-only and self-contained, and it is strictly smaller than the item: no dimension cutoff, no space, no base change. A whole-DAG search found no duplicate (by 05UA/05UD tags or by Ass+flat+specialization). I tested it on k[t,x]/(tx) at the origin (both sides non-flat), on an embedded fibre point, on M=0 and on A^2->A^1. Batch-5 check: the 7 listed citations are generic Stacks tools (02OJ/05AT, 03DX/03LC, 03D8/03G8, 03EC, 03H4/03H5, 05DC, 02JZ). A dependency search from each found no Poincare-duality, trace-transport, assumption or trace-formula node in its closure; the a1 point-calculus node reaches sec-trace-formula only through the definition def-trf-algebraic-space. So none of them is a step of the trace formula or Poincare duality. Declared tool_uses accepted as black-box generic tools. No SGA source is used.
